Traupman 104

Minimē!

no, not at all (refusing or denying)

The plain no of comedy to a question or a request; its pair is Maximē!, yes, certainly (see yes).

Other words

  • Nūllō modō!

    also used · classical · Traupman 104; Traupman 134

  • Minimē gentium! — absolutely not! not in the world

    also used · classical · Ter. Ph. 1033; Ter. Ad. 342

    (vōx cōmica: Plaut., Ter.)

  • haudquāquam — by no means, not at all

    also used · classical · Cic. de Or. 2.143: haudquāquam id est difficile Crassō (Lewis & Short s.v. haud); Ter. Heaut. 1.2.1 (Lewis & Short); Traupman 95

    An adverb within a sentence (haud quāquam, by no way whatever), not a one-word answer: for that, minimē.

Examples

  • Minimē gentium.

    Absolutely not.Ter. Ph. 1033

  • Āh, minimē gentium: nōn faciam.

    Ah, absolutely not; I won’t do it.Ter. Ad. 342

  • Cōgēs mē? — Minimē.

    “Will you force me?” “Not at all.”Ter. Ad. 193

  • At istōs rāstrōs intereā tamen appōne: nē labōrā. — Minimē.

    “But put those hoes down for now; don’t work.” “No.”Ter. Heaut. 88–89

See also of course, yes, God forbid!.
